basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; absent thumb 1/1, cleft palate 1/3 and cardiac defects 1/3 support involvement. Very small denominators limit certainty.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: absent thumb is a structural limb defect reported in 1/1 assessed patients; supplied frequency supports inclusion, with substantial uncertainty.

basis: Central and peripheral neurodegeneration defines disease. Frequent muscle wasting reflects denervation; ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic ocular damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%) but reflects denervation rather than direct skeletal muscle disease.

basis: Ear, oral/palatal and jaw/digit malformations define the syndrome; mild developmental delay is a defining associated feature. Sparse hair omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: mild developmental delay is a defining syndromic feature; three primary slots prioritize the structural ear, oral and skeletal malformations.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: micrognathia and digit anomalies are defining structural components of this malformation syndrome.

basis: Decompression bubbles occupy joint tissues and obstruct vessels. Direct spinal cord or cerebral injury occurs in roughly 30-50% of clinical cases, varying by series.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurologic decompression injury affects roughly 30-50% in clinical series; it is common but does not define every case of this umbrella condition.

basis: Gracile bones and limb/thoracic hypoplasia establish skeletal disease. Pulmonary and adrenal hypoplasia have unspecified frequencies; hydrops alone establishes no additional axis.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia is reported without frequency or evidence that it is a major diagnostic criterion; common involvement cannot be established.

basis: Hutchinson teeth and interstitial keratitis are major diagnostic stigmata; sensorineural deafness completes the defining triad. Skeletal stigmata omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: Hutchinson teeth are a major diagnostic feature of late congenital syphilis; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.ocular: primary: interstitial keratitis is a major diagnostic feature of late congenital syphilis, supporting primary ocular involvement.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease. The isolated developmental-stagnation annotation (30-79%) does not establish direct neurologic impairment in this growth disorder.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental stagnation is nonspecific in this skeletal growth disorder; the record establishes no accompanying cognitive, motor-neural or structural CNS disorder.

basis: Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury define HUS; thrombotic endothelial injury directly affects small vessels. Infection or autoimmunity is not universal across subtypes.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: defining thrombotic microangiopathy directly injures and occludes small vessels; vascular thrombosis falls within the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Inherited erythroid marrow failure; congenital thumb/upper-limb anomalies occur in roughly 30-50% of RPL11 cases. Specified renal/cardiac defects are occasional; treatment-related bone loss excluded.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: RPL11-associated congenital thumb/upper-limb malformations occur in roughly 30-50%; inclusion rests on these defects, not treatment-related osteoporosis.

basis: Limb/craniofacial dysostosis, cleft lip/palate and developmental delay define the syndrome; microtia is a defining ear malformation. Blepharophimosis omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip and palate are explicitly included in the syndrome's defining phenotype; oral and palatal structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay and microcephaly are explicitly included in the defining phenotype of this particular acrofacial dysostosis.
